title: SHAPE (Summer High School Academic Program for Engineers) - Columbia Engineering
summary: SHAPE is Columbia Engineering's pre-college summer program, offering two 3-week sessions (students may attend one or both). Each student chooses one college-level engineering course taught by Columbia faculty for the session, with options spanning robotics and autonomous driving, walking robots, biomedical engineering, intro programming, data structures and algorithms, AI and data science, solar/electrical engineering, chemical engineering, sustainable engineering, healthcare engineering, and operations research. Hands-on project work and time in Columbia's Makerspace are paired with electives, workshops on public speaking and college preparation (including sessions from Columbia undergraduate admissions), a research programming series, and support from Columbia students. Commuter and residential options are available. No college credit is awarded, but students receive a faculty letter of recommendation and a program certificate.
eligibility: Commuter option: all current high school students (freshmen through seniors). Residential option: students 16 and older, mostly reserved for U.S.-based students with a limited number of international students. Application requires 3 essays (plus 1 more for residential), most recent transcript or report card, a letter of recommendation from a math or science teacher, and a resume. Chemical Engineering course requires completed high school Chemistry. Admitted students must comply with Columbia's public health requirements.
dueDate: Application opens November 2026; deadline not yet announced (2026 cycle had rolling admissions with a Dec 22 priority deadline)

title: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship (SHIP)
summary: SHIP is a competitive, full-time paid internship combining two weeks of laboratory training with six weeks of mentored cancer and biomedical research placement, plus professional development workshops and seminars, for students with minimal prior research experience.
eligibility: Entering senior year (11th-12th grade); at least 16 by program start; strong academic background and scientific interest; must reside in the Greater Seattle area; available for the full eight weeks; no international students.

title: Georgetown Medical Immersion Academy
summary: A three-week program offering deeper immersion in introductory medical-school topics including cell biology, immunology, cardiology, and emergency medicine procedures, taught by Georgetown School of Medicine faculty and medical students.
eligibility: Minimum age 15; high school student.

title: Thomas Jefferson University SummerScience
summary: SummerScience@Jefferson is a four-week online immersive experience where students collaborate with Jefferson faculty, researchers, and postdoctoral scholars through interactive lectures and hands-on experiments investigating molecular biology, forensic science, cell biology, neuroscience, and disease mechanisms, culminating in a virtual symposium.
eligibility: High school sophomores, juniors, or seniors in the current academic year.

title: University of Florida Summer Pre-Medical Professions Program (SPMPP)
summary: A five-day immersive experience at UF College of Medicine where students shadow physicians, complete hands-on skill sessions, and work on a team-based capstone project with medical students and faculty.
eligibility: Students currently in 10th or 11th grade; no minimum GPA; U.S. students welcome, limited spots for non-Florida residents.

title: Georgetown Nursing Academy
summary: A one-week academy introducing high school students to nursing fundamentals and career specializations through faculty-led instruction and hands-on clinical experiences using a patient simulator, covering nursing foundations, healthcare ethics, and specializations like acute care and women's health.
eligibility: Minimum age 15; high school student.

title: Fred Hutch Cord Blood Transplant Internship
summary: This paid, part-time internship supports stem-cell transplantation research in clinical, laboratory, and public health contexts, with interns working directly with mentors on projects and presenting findings at conferences or events.
eligibility: High school: entering seniors, age 18+, interested in research, must be onsite in Seattle. Undergraduate/postbaccalaureate and graduate tracks have separate academic/clinical background requirements; all levels require onsite Seattle attendance.

title: Stanford Investigations in Genetics
summary: This online course examines genes, genetic variation, and heredity through an interdisciplinary lens, exploring genetic mutation, disease, microbiome composition, and experimental design in relation to biology, medicine, and evolution.
eligibility: Grades 9-11 at time of application; completion of a high school biology course.

title: Stanford Biotechnology: Innovations and Applications
summary: This Stanford Pre-Collegiate online course explores the intersection of biology, technology, and scientific innovation through biotechnology, covering molecular biology, genetics, biochemistry, and bioinformatics applications in medicine, agriculture, and industry.
eligibility: Grades 9-11 at time of application; completion of a high school biology course.

title: UC Davis Health Summer VolunTEEN
summary: A hospital and outpatient volunteer program giving students real-world experience in departments including Patient Transportation, Radiology, and Neuroscience Specialties, exploring potential healthcare careers.
eligibility: Minimum age 16 by program start; two references (at least one from school personnel); signed parent/guardian permission; required vaccinations (MMR, Varicella, Tdap) and TB testing.

title: UCSC Extension High School Healthcare Academy
summary: This academy introduces high school students to healthcare and STEM fields through hands-on labs, mentorship from health professionals, and a formal human biology course earning UC credit, culminating in a capstone project.
eligibility: Motivated students in grades 9-12 (as of Spring 2026); curiosity about science and interest in healthcare careers.

title: Stony Brook Lab Techniques in Biotechnology
summary: This program introduces high school students to techniques and equipment used in modern biotechnology research through hands-on work with model organisms, including bacterial transformations, gel electrophoresis, PCR analysis, and DNA/RNA extraction.
eligibility: Completion of NYS Living Environment curriculum (biology background required); chemistry background suggested; must complete ninth grade before the program starts.

title: Hormel Institute High School Summer Research Scholars
summary: This onsite biomedical research program immerses high school students in lab techniques and data analysis at The Hormel Institute, with a research portfolio and professional development activities.
eligibility: Students entering grades 11-12 or recent (class of 2026) graduates; minimum 3.5 GPA; completed biology course; letter of recommendation from a science or math instructor.

title: CDC Museum Online Summer Course
summary: A web-based course with synchronous and asynchronous components educating high school students on public health topics including epidemiology, global health, infectious and chronic disease, and emergency preparedness.
eligibility: High school students during the summer before junior or senior year; at least 16 years old on the first day of the course.

title: Lundquist Institute STAR High School Program
summary: The STAR High School Program is an eight-week summer research experience where students conduct individual projects alongside physicians and scientists at the Lundquist Institute, culminating in a research presentation and stipend.
eligibility: High school junior or senior (as of Fall 2026) at a Los Angeles County school; outstanding general academic achievement with a focus on science coursework; full participation required (max three absences).

title: SIU Pathways to Saluki Medicine
summary: An overnight residential camp hosted by SIU School of Medicine's Physiology Department giving high school students hands-on learning in anatomy and physiology and interaction with healthcare professionals, including cadaver lab tours and clinical skills instruction.
eligibility: High school students entering grades 10, 11, or 12; interest in medicine or biomedical science; must commit to the full 5-day residential program.

title: Scripps Research REACH Internship
summary: The REACH high school internship gives students hands-on laboratory research experience and mentorship at Scripps Research, working full-time alongside scientist mentors and attending weekly professional development workshops.
eligibility: Must attend one of nine designated San Diego County partner schools; at least 16 years old; completed one year each of high school chemistry and biology; minimum 3.0 GPA; San Diego County resident; legally eligible to work in the U.S.; cannot have participated in REACH before.

title: Mass General Brigham Aspiring Physician and Medical Scientist Program
summary: This program gives high school students hands-on healthcare and medical research experience with instruction from Mass General Brigham and Harvard Medical School faculty, including clinical simulations across specialties like surgery, emergency medicine, and pediatrics.
eligibility: No formal prerequisites; program targets motivated, high-achieving students interested in medicine or medical research careers; applications reviewed by faculty committee.

title: UC Irvine Summer Online Research Program
summary: A three-week mentored remote program that increases high school students' exposure to research methods, covering evidence-based medicine, literature evaluation, and research report writing, culminating in submitting an abstract to a national conference.
eligibility: Ages 15-18; minimum unweighted GPA of 3.3; interest in healthcare research; priority to students in higher grades.

title: Tulane Genomic Insights
summary: A hands-on genetics course where students learn how genes and proteins determine traits through molecular laboratory work including DNA extraction, PCR, and DNA digestion, applying these skills to analyze their own genetic material and investigate seafood mislabeling.
eligibility: Students in grades 11-12.

title: FIU Junior Doctors of Tomorrow (JDOT)
summary: A week-long enrichment program at FIU's Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine giving high school students clinical workshops, interactive sessions, and mentorship with medical professionals to explore healthcare careers.
eligibility: Rising juniors or seniors; minimum 3.0 GPA; 500-word essay, teacher/counselor recommendation, and transcript required; limited to 30 students per session.

title: Columbia YES in THE HEIGHTS
summary: YES in the Heights is a two-year, paid cancer research internship where students work with faculty mentors at Columbia University Medical Center, attend journal clubs, and build research skills, aimed at increasing the pool of youth entering STEM fields.
eligibility: U.S. citizen or permanent resident; at least 14 years old; good academic standing with demonstrated science aptitude; must commit to 8 weeks in person, 8 hours daily; priority to students from HICCC's service area or prior participants; highly competitive (<10% acceptance).

title: Emory Healthcare VolunTEEN
summary: This program places high school students in hospital and clinic departments across the Emory Healthcare system for meaningful volunteer service, offering firsthand insight into healthcare careers.
eligibility: High school students aged 16-18 by June 1, 2026.

title: UC Irvine Summer Healthcare Experience
summary: A career exploration and empowerment program for students interested in healthcare careers, focused on equitable healthcare and reducing leadership disparities in medicine, held full-day and in-person at UC Irvine Medical Center.
eligibility: High school students aged 16-18 who will be rising juniors or seniors; must have turned 16 by program start; interest in pursuing healthcare careers.

title: Children's Hospital Los Angeles High School Summer Volunteer Program
summary: Volunteers provide direct service to patients, families, and staff at Children's Hospital Los Angeles, including escorting and greeting patients, across a structured multi-week commitment.
eligibility: Ages 15-17 by program start; completed freshman year; commit to 16 hours weekly across four time blocks; full immunization records, negative TB screening, and drug/alcohol screening clearance required.

title: Moffitt High School Internship in Integrated Mathematical Oncology (HIP-IMO)
summary: HIP-IMO is a ten-week research internship at Moffitt Cancer Center combining mathematics and biology for interdisciplinary cancer research alongside leading scientists.
eligibility: Check program website for current eligibility details; not fully specified on the page fetched.

title: Astera Summer High School Oncology Research Experience (ASHORE)
summary: ASHORE lets students work on real oncology research projects under physician mentorship, with clinical projects, specialized lectures, physician shadowing, and potential national-conference presentations, in a hybrid in-person/remote format.
eligibility: Completed 9th grade or higher; completed 1 year of biology; demonstrated significant interest in cancer and medical research.

title: UCLA NeuroCamp
summary: NeuroCamp is a free UCLA summer course introducing a small cohort of motivated high school students to foundational concepts and lab techniques in molecular neurobiology, neurophysiology, and neuroanatomy.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12; must reside in Los Angeles County; required to attend the full program (no partial participation).

title: UT Tyler Summer Medical Programs
summary: UT Tyler School of Medicine offers three distinct summer tracks for high schoolers: the Pathways SUPERNet Summer Medical Scholars Academy (five-day residential healthcare-career overview for 9th-11th graders), the Summer Research and Clinical Externship (two-week research and shadowing experience for seniors and college students), and Pre-Med Camp (admissions/interview prep with clinical and research exposure for economically disadvantaged East Texas-area juniors/seniors). May need to be split into separate entries given differing eligibility and formats.
eligibility: Varies by track: Medical Scholars Academy open to current 9th-11th graders; Research/Clinical Externship open to HS seniors through college juniors in good academic standing; Pre-Med Camp open to economically disadvantaged rising juniors/seniors (or homeschooled) with East Texas ties.

title: Rockefeller Summer Neuroscience Program (SNP)
summary: SNP is a two-week course for New York City public high schoolers led by Rockefeller graduate students, featuring interactive lectures, scientific article presentations, original experiment design, brain dissection, and facility tours, with all expenses covered.
eligibility: Must be enrolled in a New York City public school; at least 16 years old by program start; motivated, mature, and curious students, regardless of grades or experience; program particularly welcomes students with limited prior science opportunities.

title: MIT-Weill Cornell HIP-SAT
summary: HIP-SAT places homeschooled high school students in eight-week paid research internships in MIT or Weill Cornell Medicine labs, with mentorship from PhD students and postdocs across chemical biology, chemistry, and engineering, culminating in an August symposium.
location: Cambridge MA or New York NY
eligibility: Homeschooled high school students; must be local to Cambridge/Boston or NYC, or arrange own local housing (program does not provide/supervise housing).

title: UCSF CURE Research Internship
summary: The CURE Research Internship is an eight-week summer program where high school juniors and community college students conduct original research at UCSF under faculty and graduate mentor guidance, exploring biomedical career paths across multiple disciplines and presenting findings at a closing symposium.
eligibility: Current 11th grader or current City College of San Francisco student; at least 16 by program start; minimum 2.5 GPA; completed Biology or Chemistry with a grade of B or better; able to commit 40 hours/week for 8 weeks.

title: Salk High School Summer Scholars (Heithoff-Brody)
summary: The Salk Institute's Heithoff-Brody High School Summer Scholars Program is an eight-week paid internship where students work alongside Salk scientists on original research projects, with lab work, seminars, industry visits, and a closing research symposium.
eligibility: San Diego County resident attending high school in the county; at least 16 by program start; minimum 2.75 GPA; completed at least one high school biology course; applicants under 18 need a work permit; chemistry coursework and reliable transportation preferred.

title: Boston University BLAST
summary: BLAST is a paid internship featuring problem-based learning and laboratory practicums that build scientific literacy and readiness for college-level science coursework, with mentorship from undergraduate, graduate, and medical students.
eligibility: Rising high school junior, senior, or graduating senior with demonstrated interest in science; honors or advanced STEM coursework preferred.

title: Georgetown Medical Academy
summary: A one-week residential or commuter program introducing high school students to medicine through lectures, interactive experiences, and group discussions covering anatomy, physiology, radiology, surgery, cancer, and biomedical ethics, with hands-on suturing, casting, dissections, and simulator work.
eligibility: Minimum age 15; high school student.

title: Texas A&M BioFORCE
summary: BioFORCE is a hands-on STEM summer program introducing high school students to biomanufacturing through facility tours, lectures, labs, and industry professional interactions, offered as a residential camp in College Station or a commuter camp in Dallas.
location: College Station TX or Dallas TX
eligibility: Students in grades 9-12; at least 15 years old.

title: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
summary: An interdisciplinary in-person day camp at CDC headquarters immersing high school students in public health topics including epidemiology, infectious and chronic disease, and emergency preparedness through a fast-paced, academically demanding curriculum.
eligibility: High school students during the summer before junior or senior year; at least 16 years old on the first day of camp.

title: Campbell University BIOS²
summary: BIOS² (Biotechnology, Inquiry, Outreach, and STEM2) is a residential week-long program letting students explore health sciences through laboratory work, workshops, and campus experiences, investigating careers in biotech, pharmacology, and related fields.
eligibility: Rising 9th through 12th grade high school students.

title: Memorial Sloan Kettering Summer Student Program
summary: This eight-week biomedical or computational lab-based internship pairs high school juniors with mentors at MSK's Manhattan campus for a self-directed research project, alongside professional development events exploring translational medicine.
eligibility: Current high school juniors only; permanent address within 25 miles of MSK's Upper East Side Manhattan location; minimum 3.5 GPA in science subjects; at least 14 by June 2026; legally authorized to work in the U.S.; able to commit to all eight weeks.

title: Duke University Neuroscience Experience (DUNE)
summary: DUNE is a full-time summer research program engaging local high school students in neuroscience labs at Duke University, with hands-on research mentorship, professional development workshops, and a stipend.
eligibility: Current high school sophomores or juniors attending one of 16 specified Durham, NC public/charter schools; at least 16 by June 15, 2026; reliable daily transportation to Duke; U.S. citizen, national, or legal resident.

title: Drexel Public Health Institute for Leadership & Advocacy (PHILA)
summary: PHILA is a one-week academic program exploring public health career paths, where students engage with field experts, visit local health organizations, and develop solutions to real-world public health challenges in Philadelphia.
eligibility: High school juniors and seniors within commuting distance of Drexel's campus; interest in public health, medicine, healthcare, law, communications, environmental sciences, policy, sociology, or psychology.

title: University of Houston Mohanlab Summer Internship (MLSI)
summary: MLSI offers rising seniors eight weeks of bench research in biomedical sciences, bioengineering, big data analytics, and neuroscience at MohanLab, including initial lab-technique instruction, mentored research, and a closing presentation.
eligibility: Rising seniors (completed 11th grade); strong academic track record preferred; interest in biomedical, bioengineering, or computer science fields.

title: Loma Linda ABC High School Program
summary: The Apprenticeship Bridge to College (ABC) Program is a full-time summer internship in health disparities research for Inland Empire high school students, combining hands-on biomedical research with seminars on health disparities and scientific/communication skill-building.
eligibility: Talented Inland Empire (Southern California) high school students; see program's 'Who Can Apply' page for full criteria.

title: Experiences in Research (EinR) - Berkeley Lab
summary: Paid six-week summer internship at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory where high schoolers work directly with Berkeley Lab professionals on real projects in STEM and STEM-adjacent fields. Project areas include experimental research and data collection, data science (coding and non-coding), coding-dependent projects, and administration/science communication. Students review a project booklet and rank their top three choices when applying. Interns work roughly 30-35 hours per week; projects are hybrid or virtual depending on the host office. Goals include building mentor connections, professional STEM skills, and experience in science communication and collaboration.
location: Berkeley CA (hybrid or virtual depending on project)
eligibility: Current 10th, 11th, or 12th graders enrolled in Northern California schools, with experience doing independent work. Must be at least 16 by the mid-June program start; must meet both age and grade requirements. All Northern California applicants reviewed, but priority given to students within ~30 miles of Berkeley Lab. Former interns not eligible. Oakland USD students must also complete the ECCCO common application.

title: Online Summer - Columbia University
summary: Columbia University's Online Summer program lets high school students take rigorous, collaborative courses with Columbia instructors through an interactive virtual learning platform, choosing from over 40 courses across a dozen subject areas in 1- or 2-week sessions.
eligibility: Open to students entering grades 9-12
dueDate: Priority deadline: Feb 1, Regular deadline: Apr 1

title: College Edge Summer - Columbia University
summary: Columbia University's College Edge Summer program allows high school students to earn college credit by enrolling in real Columbia undergraduate courses (from a pre-approved list) on the Morningside campus, alongside academic advisement and professional development opportunities.
eligibility: Students in grades 11-12

title: Academy for iOS App Development - UT Austin
summary: A 6-day residential academy teaching high school students to build mobile apps using Swift and Xcode, with a focus on user interface design, programming logic, and collaboration. Students must bring their own MacBook Air or Pro (13-inch or larger). Program is set to return for Summer 2027; not currently accepting applications.
eligibility: Entering grades 10-12 (Fall 2026); intermediate programming level required (prior experience with C++, Java, or Python)

title: Berkeley Summer Computer Science Academy
summary: A two-week immersive residential program for high school students interested in computer science and AI, based on UC Berkeley's "Beauty and Joy of Computing" curriculum, using the visual programming language Snap! to explore core CS concepts and AI topics.
eligibility: Completed 10th or 11th grade by program start; age 16-17 by June 21, 2026; minimum 3.0 GPA; domestic and international students welcome (English proficiency required for international applicants); must live in on-campus housing

title: Academy for Game Development - UT Austin
summary: A residential, overnight academy where high school students code their own game while exploring the creative and technical sides of game development (using Godot/GDScript), meeting UT faculty and industry professionals, and learning about career pathways.
eligibility: Entering grades 10-12 (Fall 2026); beginner-level programming or above

title: AI & Health Summer High School Bootcamp - MIT Jameel Clinic
summary: A one-week, in-person bootcamp introducing high school students to artificial intelligence and machine learning methods used in clinical AI and drug discovery, through daily instruction (7+ hours), group projects, and hands-on learning.
eligibility: Incoming sophomores, juniors, and seniors (grades 10-12); international students not eligible for financial aid, no visa sponsorship available
dueDate: Priority deadline: Nov 1, Regular deadline: Feb 22

title: UC Berkeley M.E.T. Innovation Academy (M.E.T.ia)
summary: A residential summer program combining engineering and business education for high school students interested in technology and entrepreneurship, featuring lectures, lab visits, guest speakers, Silicon Valley field visits, a capstone project, and a pitch competition.
eligibility: Rising junior or senior; strong aptitude for math and science; demonstrated interest in the intersection of technology and business

title: SHTEM: Summer Internships for High Schoolers - Stanford
summary: An unpaid research internship placing high school juniors/seniors and community college students in small mentored groups (2-5 students) on interdisciplinary research spanning information science, engineering, computer science, biology, neuroscience, psychology, linguistics, design, and philosophy. Students work 20-30 hours weekly.
eligibility: High school junior or senior in the 2026-2027 school year; minimum age 14 by June 20, 2027; U.S. citizen or permanent resident only; no prior research experience required

title: DSI Summer Lab - University of Chicago
summary: An 8-week paid summer research program pairing Chicago-area high school students and undergraduates with data science mentors on applied, interdisciplinary research spanning social science, climate and energy policy, public policy, materials science, and biomedical research. No prior research experience required.
eligibility: Undergraduate students and Chicago-area high school students; high school applicants must reside year-round in the Chicago area

title: ARISE (Applied Research Innovations in Science and Engineering) - NYU
summary: A free 10-week program combining 4 weeks of safety training, college writing workshops, and research skills development with placement in one of 80+ NYU research labs assisting faculty on real-world projects. Includes a $2,000 participation stipend.
eligibility: Rising junior or senior; must be a full-time NYC resident attending an NYC school

title: Stanford Tri-Valley Clinical Academy
summary: A community-based academy giving high school students an active introduction to the practice of medicine, combining clinical skills training (suturing, knot tying) with practical experience (vitals, history and physical exams) alongside Stanford faculty, community physicians, and hospital staff.

title: Sci-Fi Medicine (Graphic Medicine, Comics, and Imagination) - Stanford
summary: A two-week in-person course exploring how speculative storytelling and visual narratives shape understanding of the human body, illness, technology, and care, through graphic novels, comics, and science fiction; students create original medical comics or speculative scenarios.

title: Stanford Suturing Bootcamp
summary: An intensive two-day surgical skills program progressing from basic suturing techniques to advanced closure patterns, with expert-guided hands-on training, simulation models, and career panels. No prior suturing experience required.
eligibility: Minimum age 16; interest in medical careers; no prior suturing experience required

title: Cardiothoracic Surgical Skills Summer Internship - Stanford
summary: An intensive course providing high school students knowledge of and hands-on exposure to basic and advanced cardiothoracic surgery, including knot tying, dissection, suturing, and surgical procedures, taught by Stanford faculty, surgical residents, and staff.
eligibility: High school students considering careers in science and medicine; full daily attendance required

title: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP)
summary: A five-week immersive enrichment program exposing high school juniors from underrepresented, low-income, and first-generation backgrounds to health science and medicine, with mentorship and college preparation support.
eligibility: High school juniors; low-income and/or first-generation college background; Northern California residents

title: Pediatrics Internship Program at Stanford (PIPS)
summary: A 7-week summer internship where high school students learn about science, medicine, and pediatric/maternal-child health research careers, with opportunities to conduct research projects under Stanford faculty mentorship.
eligibility: Rising junior or senior; minimum age 16 by program start; must reside and attend school in the San Francisco Bay Area (SF, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Marin, Alameda, Contra Costa, or Santa Cruz counties); minimum 3.0 unweighted GPA; must commit to full 7 weeks

title: Stanford Clinical Summer Internship (CSI)
summary: A pre-medical clinical training program for high school and undergraduate students, offered in multiple formats: a two-week on-campus session, a two-week virtual session, or a 10-week fall virtual intensive (weekly 90-minute sessions), covering hands-on clinical skills and exposure to the practice of medicine.
eligibility: Rising high school juniors and seniors, and undergraduate pre-medical students

title: Clinical Anatomy Summer Program (CASP) - Stanford
summary: A week-long, full-day, non-residential course introducing high school students to human anatomy through lectures, hands-on lab work, surgical observations, and physician-led workshops.
eligibility: Minimum age 15 at program start; COVID-19 vaccination required; high school transcript submission required

title: Stanford Anesthesia Summer Institute (SASI)
summary: A clinical science summer program exploring anesthesiology, technology, and healthcare careers through hands-on simulation training, patient-voice engagement, and mentorship. Offered in multiple formats: SASI Foundations (two-week on-campus with capstone), SASI Clinical Skills (one-week on-campus), and SASI Virtual (online).
eligibility: Open to high school and undergraduate students; no GPA or test score minimums stated

title: RAMP UP/STaRS Internship Program - Stanford
summary: An 8-week, fully funded research internship in reconstructive surgery and dental regenerative medicine, introducing high school and community college students to biomedical/clinical research through mentorship, lab technique training, workshops, and a final presentation showcase. No prior lab experience required.
eligibility: High school and community college students of all backgrounds; no prior laboratory experience required

title: Tech-X: Mental Health and Technology Immersion Experience - Stanford
summary: A one-week summer program exploring the intersection of mental health and technology through Stanford faculty seminars on digital mental health tools, social media, and AI's impact on wellbeing, hands-on learning, lab visits, and a group capstone project.
eligibility: High school students

title: Mock Trial Institute - UCLA
summary: A one-week immersive mock trial program run by the UCLA Mock Trial program (UCLA Anderson School of Management), taught by UCLA professors, coaches, and alumni. Students learn case theory, witness examination, and opening/closing statements through team workshops, hear from a Careers in Law panel, and compete in a final tournament judged by real lawyers and judges. Offered as in-person sessions (with UCLA residence hall housing) or a one-week online session.
eligibility: Ages 15-18 (must be 15 by session start); minimum 3.0 GPA; no prior mock trial experience required; proof of age and recent transcript required

title: AI-Enabled Entrepreneurship - Startup UCLA
summary: A 5-module, self-paced online course where students use AI tools to conduct market research and build a usable prototype for a startup idea.
eligibility: Grades 10-12; minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA
dueDate: Rolling admissions year-round; in-person Summer 2027 track opens applications Feb 2027

title: Social Entrepreneurship Institute - Startup UCLA
summary: A 10-module, self-paced online course where students identify a social problem, build a venture model, and develop a pitch for a social impact venture.
eligibility: Grades 10-12; minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA
dueDate: Rolling admissions year-round; in-person Summer 2027 track opens applications Feb 2027

title: SF Public Defender Internship
summary: The San Francisco Public Defender's Office offers a paid internship (through the Opportunities for All program) for students and young adults, providing exposure to public defender work and office experience across Downtown, Youth Defender, and MAGIC program locations.
eligibility: Ages 13-24; must commit to at least 8 hours per week for 3 months; no resume or cover letter required

title: Architecture Career Workshop - CalPoly

summary: Two-week interactive mock trial camp at University of the Pacific (Session 2) run by the McGeorge Mock Trial Team; students work through simulated case files and courtroom exercises.
eligibility: High school students passionate about law

title: CARE AI - Stanford
summary: A focused two-week summer program for high-school students interested in AI applied to Asian health outcomes and underserved communities, combining technology and health equity
location: Stanford University campus, Palo Alto, CA (day program, no housing)
eligibility: Rising high school sophomores, juniors, or seniors; at least 14 years old; must live within commuting distance of Stanford's Palo Alto campus.

title: Sports Industry Academy - UCSB
summary: The Sports Industry Academy, works closely with top sports executives, corporations and educational institutions in preparing our future sports industry leaders.
eligibility: Mature, highly talented California community college, high school, and university scholars from diverse backgrounds; no formal GPA/test criteria published

title: USC Pre-College
summary: Various courses in business, communications, engineering, global studies, health sciences, and the humanities.
eligibility: Completed at least 9th grade; rigorous high school curriculum. Domestic deadline May 8, 2026; international deadline March 13, 2026 (international students need English proficiency test or waiver)

title: Institute for Mathematics and Democracy
summary: Students work in groups analyzing real-life data as it relates to political and social issues.
eligibility: Advanced high school students

summary: This is a complete list of high school programs through Stanford Medicine.

summary: A two weeks program where students learn game design fundamentals + C# + Unity scripting as part of teams.
eligibility: Students entering sophomore, junior, or senior year of high school in Fall 2026; intermediate coding skills with at least one formal coding class completed at B+ or higher
dueDate: Applications Open: Early Jan; Deadline: TBD

summary: You will code and design your first video game prototype using Unity3D. Coursework includes C# programming with Unity3D, 2D pixel art and sprite animation, digital music and sound FX, and narrative writing.
location: In-person (Urban Arts Learning Lab) or Remote (Discord)
eligibility: Students entering 10th-12th grade in Fall 2026; no prior experience required

summary: A two-week immersive program that blends medical science with video game design, ideal for high-school students who are creative and curious about health innovation. Participants design health-focused video games and present their work at a final symposium.

summary: Provides a rigorous, college-level investigation of emerging financial technologies, enabling students to grasp the inner workings of Bitcoin, prepare for an AI-based economy and think like entrepreneurs.

summary: Online math courses including competitive math preparation.
eligibility: Students in grades 5-12

title: Fusion Academy Summer Programs - Fusion Academy
summary: Fusion Academy’s summer school programs are personalized 1‑to‑1 and small group options that help students catch up get ahead or explore new interests
eligibility: Middle and high school students
